text: In headless mode (`claude -p`), a conductor driver can launch the generated Workflow as a BACKGROUND task and then end its turn ('the run will notify me when it completes') — but ending the turn exits the -p process, killing the orphaned workflow. Observed live 2026-07-14 in an arena cell (uglify-corner-cases, opus-4-8[1m]/high): flawless Setup (DoD frozen, verify-reports.cjs grounded, per-report workers planned), then Workflow launched backgrounded, driver ended turn at ~17.5 min, process exited, wf/ branch left with ZERO commits, cell scored failed. Reproduced 2/2 on the same cell (attempts 1029s/1050s, both wf/ branches zero-commit); the same day five SHORT cells completed fine — the driver backgrounds the workflow precisely when it anticipates a LONG run, so the bug bites hardest on the hardest tasks. SKILL.md should pin the invocation: run the Workflow with run_in_background: false (or explicitly forbid ending the turn while the workflow runs — poll/wait until Finalize completes) whenever the session is non-interactive. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): SKILL.md (or the scaffold's driver instructions) contains an explicit run_in_background/do-not-end-turn directive for the Workflow invocation; today it says nothing, leaving the driver free to orphan the run.

Conductor loses to a RAW single session on wide, decomposable tasks because its generated plan runs independent work items as SEQUENTIAL phases. Measured head-to-head 2026-07-14 on arena task uglify-corner-cases (six INDEPENDENT compiler bugs, cellCapSec=3600): raw sonnet-5 one-shot RESOLVED 6/6 in ~53 min; opus-4-8[1m]/high + conductor TIMED OUT at 3603s with only 2/6 fixed — its driver designed Setup -> DoDBaseline -> Report1..Report6 -> DoDGate and paid worker spin-up + a ~5-min full-suite verification per phase, serially. The six reports were embarrassingly parallel (disjoint transforms, one shared file but separable hunks; a per-worker worktree already exists). SKILL.md / the scaffold should instruct: when the frozen DoD decomposes into independent criteria, fan the workers out concurrently (Workflow parallel()/pipeline over per-criterion workers, verify once at the gate), reserving sequential phases for genuinely dependent steps. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): generate a plan for a task whose DoD has N independent checkable criteria and assert the emitted loop runs their workers inside one parallel()/pipeline stage rather than N sequential phase() blocks; today the scaffold emits strictly sequential phases.

The --independent parallel fan-out (added by whetstone run conductor-20260714-182449) is unusable for the most common real shape of independent work: N independent changes that touch the SAME FILE. Proven live 2026-07-15 (true-v2 head-to-head, improved skill verifiably loaded via --plugin-dir): the driver read the new guidance, then correctly declined the flag — 'all six fixes touch lib/compress.js, so parallel editing would clobber' — because parallel workers share ONE worktree. SKILL.md's guidance ('no shared state') excludes shared-file tasks, so conductor stays sequential exactly where parallelism matters most (arena measured: sequential conductor times out at 3600s where a raw session resolves in ~53min). Fix: give --independent per-worker isolation — each parallel worker gets its OWN worktree/branch off the base, and a merge step (sequential rebase/cherry-pick with conflict-fix loop, or diff-level merge) combines them before the gates verify the combined diff once. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): generate with --independent and assert the emitted parallel workers are each instructed to work in a DISTINCT worktree (not the shared one) and that a merge/integrate step exists between the parallel Work phase and the gate; today all parallel workers share the single worktree and no merge step is emitted.

Even with SKILL.md pinning run_in_background:false + do-not-end-turn (kept fix from run conductor-20260714-182449, verifiably loaded), a headless opus driver STILL ended its run with the workflow unfinished: final message said 'I'm holding my turn open until the workflow finishes... Waiting for completion' and the -p process then exited at ~25min with only the setup harness committed (observed 2026-07-15, true-v2 cell). Saying it does not make it so: the driver must not emit a final text message at all while the workflow runs — the reliable pattern in -p mode is to invoke the Workflow tool with run_in_background:false so the TOOL CALL ITSELF blocks until completion, and SKILL.md should say exactly that (the tool call blocks; do not launch backgrounded and narrate waiting). Consider also instructing the driver to verify workflow status from .workflows/state/<name>.json AFTER the Workflow tool returns and before finalizing. Discriminating check is behavioral (claude -p A/B per the repo's proof norm): a headless run on a multi-phase task must end with the workflow state file status=complete/failed and a non-empty wf/ branch, not status=running; as a cheap structural proxy (RED now): SKILL.md's launch section must state that the foreground Workflow call blocks and that the driver must not end its turn with narration while status=running.

A judged-tier DoD criterion can be satisfied (or waved through as 'deferred') on the strength of worker reports alone. Observed live: spec required TOTP, DoDGate ran, the main agent relayed 'feature was deferred', and not a single line of TOTP code existed — the deferral was a unilateral scope change made by a step inside the workflow, and every report-reading layer confirmed it. Two-layer fix: (1) DoD acquisition (SKILL.md step 1c) should bias criteria toward the checkable tier by compiling them into executable checks (e.g. failing-first tests via lirbox-test-writer, RED at DoDBaseline) so 'deferred' is a red check, not a slippable status; (2) the DoDGate worker prompt for judged-tier criteria must require verification against the actual diff/artifacts in the worktree, explicitly treat worker reports/implementation-notes as untrusted claims, and hard-fail any criterion whose implementation was 'deferred'/'descoped' without a human decision recorded in the DoD file. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): generate a delivery workflow with a judged criterion and assert the emitted DoDGate prompt contains artifact-evidence + reports-are-untrusted + deferral-fails directives; today it has none of them.

When DoDGate finds unmet criteria after its 3 in-phase rounds, the generated conductor throws ('DoDGate failed: DoD not fully met') and the run dies — there is no outer verify-loop. The whole run's work is stranded one phase from done, and the only recovery is a human restarting. The generator should emit a bounded plan-execute-verify outer loop around Implement..DoDGate: on gate failure, a Replan phase receives the exact unmet criteria (ids + check output) and produces a new immutable plan version, execution re-runs, the gate re-runs; capped at N attempts (default 2); stall detection — if the unmet-criteria set is unchanged between two consecutive gate runs, stop early; every exit that is not gate-green escalates (state.json status 'escalated' with the unmet list and plan-version history) instead of throwing. Routing decisions must consume only executed check results, never worker reports. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): generate a delivery workflow and assert the script contains a replan/attempt loop with an attempt cap and an unchanged-unmet-set early-stop around the DoDGate, and that gate failure sets an escalated state rather than only throwing; today the gate is single-pass + throw.

--model-mode's default is backwards. `auto` (tier each worker by phase class: haiku for mechanical Setup/checkpoint/Verify/PR/TicketUpdate, the think model + effort:'high' for gates/RED/Writeup, the work model for --phases) is what we want on essentially every run, but it must be opted into — so real runs silently inherit the session model everywhere and pay a strong model on mechanical checkpoint/Setup/PR workers. Flip it: `auto` becomes the DEFAULT (no flag needed), and the old inherit-the-session-model behavior (emit NO `model:`/`effort:` opt at all) moves to `--model-mode inherit`. The literal `--model-mode default` must now HARD-ERROR pointing at `inherit` — keeping it as a silent alias would leave the flag value named 'default' meaning the non-default. The --model-think/--model-work guard inverts: they are valid with no mode flag (auto is default) and must be REJECTED under `--model-mode inherit`. Also update: the generator's stdout mode echo, references/generator-flags.md, SKILL.md, and scripts/snapshots/ (regenerate via test-scaffold.cjs --update-snapshots; renaming the misleading snapshots/default.js to inherit.js is fine). NOTE ON THE SURFACE: scripts/test-scaffold.cjs carries a 'default emits no model opt (byte-cost-free)' assertion pinning the OLD default — RETARGETING that assertion to pin `inherit` byte-cost-free is explicitly authorized and REQUIRED; deleting or weakening it is not. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): (a) generate with NO --model-mode flag and assert the emitted script carries model:'haiku' on Setup + checkpoint + PR, the think model with effort:'high' on CodeGate/RED, and the work model on the --phases workers; (b) generate with --model-mode inherit and assert NO `model:` and no `effort:` opt appears anywhere in the emitted script; (c) assert `--model-mode default` exits non-zero and its stderr names `inherit`; (d) assert --model-think with no mode flag exits ZERO while --model-think under --model-mode inherit exits non-zero. Today (a) emits zero model opts and (d) is exactly inverted.

The --independent fan-out is now mechanically sound (per-worker worktrees + integrate step, kept by run conductor-20260719-220515 / PR #34) but drivers still almost never pass it — observed 2026-07-25 across real usage: ~100% of generated workflows are strictly linear, no parallel() anywhere. This is a DECISION gap, not a mechanism gap. SKILL.md step 1b triages a tier and step 1c acquires a DoD, but NO step ever enumerates the work items or their dependency edges, and --independent survives only as a passive aside inside one paragraph of step 2 ('when the work items are independent, add --independent'). With sequential as the unstated default and no artifact forcing the question, the driver takes the linear path every time — which is exactly the shape arena measured losing to a raw single session on wide decomposable tasks (uglify-corner-cases: sequential conductor timed out at 3600s vs ~53min raw). Fix in SKILL.md: add a REQUIRED decompose step (a new step 1d, positioned BEFORE the generate step) in which the driver emits a work-item table with an explicit per-item 'depends on: <item ids | none>' declaration, plus the hard rule that every item whose dependency list is 'none' MUST be emitted in ONE --independent fan-out, with sequential --phases reserved for items carrying a declared dependency edge. Step 2's --independent paragraph must then reference that table instead of restating a soft heuristic, so the flag choice is read off a declared artifact rather than re-judged. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): assert SKILL.md contains a required decompose step that (a) names a per-item dependency declaration, (b) states a MUST rule binding no-dependency items to a single --independent fan-out, and (c) appears BEFORE the 'Generate the conductor' step; and that step 2's --independent paragraph cross-references it. Today SKILL.md has no decomposition step, no dependency declaration, and no MUST rule. NOTE: this is a structural proxy for a behavioral outcome — the real proof is an arena A/B of driver flag-choice across skill versions, currently blocked by arena's missing --plugin-dir/skill-version axis (filed separately in feedback/arena.jsonl).
